key_insight: First-principles calculations predict β-TeO₃ as an n-type semiconductor with a band gap above 3 eV and ultrahigh work functions reaching approximately 8 eV.
engineering_relevance: These properties could enable hole injection, extraction, and transport layers or transparent electrodes in photovoltaic and light-emitting devices.
method: Calculate electronic properties and impurity-induced carrier doping.
Assess point defects, including oxygen vacancies and shallow donors.
Evaluate work functions across low-index nonpolar surfaces.
evidence_signal: Calculations identify interstitial H, Li, Na, Cu, Mg, and Zn and substitutional F as shallow donors, while surface oxygen vacancies are energetically favored and tend to lower work functions.
watch_item: Experimental validation is needed, and controlling oxygen chemical potential will be important to suppress surface vacancies and preserve high work functions.
paper_title: Tellurium trioxide as an n-type wide-gap semiconductor with ultrahigh work functions from first principles
